title: The Leverage Trap: Why Working Harder Keeps You Broke

scenes.narration: You can work sixteen hours a day for your entire life and still stay broke, because effort alone hits a hard ceiling.
When you trade hours for dollars, every dollar costs a piece of your life you never get back.
That is why the wealthy are not working harder than you. They are playing a completely different game.
The game is leverage: disconnecting how hard you work from how much you produce.
Historically, leverage meant labor or capital, both requiring someone else's permission. Today, code and media require none.
Write a line of code or record one video, and it reaches a million people for the exact same effort as reaching one.
For the first time in history, your systems can work twenty-four hours a day, even while you sleep.
Small leveraged actions do not just add up. They trigger cascades where every piece knocks over something twice its size.
Hard work gives you a linear slope. Leverage gives you escape velocity.
Stop renting out your hours. Build something that works without you.
